Car Works. Painters and others as will be suggested by your directory.
The rebate does not apply to wood alcohol.
AS TO STAMPS.
We think that the court will admit record and parol evidence to prove
the amount of alcohol used since August 28th, 1894. Though recovery of stamps
from distillers and others might be accepted, subject of course to corrobora-
tive proof. They should be cautioned to keep careful account hereafter These
claims are growing DAILY. Alcohol being kept directly under Governnent super-
vision, we will in many instances have a chain of record evidence.
AS TO THE AMOUNT.
Tax on alcohol is $1.10 gallon, 100 proof, but each gallon is about
188 proof.
SMALL CLAIMS.
Easily procured, and the charge should be 25%. Ve would adviseyou to
take VERY large claims even if at the rate of 10%, when no larger contingent
fee can be agreed upon.
AS-TO LEGISLATION.
In event of repeal, the alcohol used for compounding from August
28th, 1894, to date of repeal, will nevertheless be entitled to rebate. The
Government cannot, we content, escape it. The Secretary's letter estimated the
amount as $10,000,000. It is not in our opinion at all probable, that a bill
will ever be passed to cover these cases without recourse to Court of Claims.
Our experience justifies this statement. Similar action was sought in the
letter-carrier cases but failed. The claims will go in form of judgments, and
the Court of Claims, will fix the amounts, otherwise special proceedings, expen-
sive to the Government would have to be inaugurated.
We can, we believe, name a party in Boston, if desired, whose share of
fees
in Letter-carrier cases, with but little effort on his part netted him
about $20.000. He co-operated with a Washington firm.
Do not be discouraged if you should find others at work in same line.
The field is a big one and will pay.
Please advise us frankly and fully from time to time, and we will be
happy to lend you every assistance possible.
As claims will be paid in order of filing and completion, prompt
action on part of USER is advisable.
